# njoagleod-api

This is the source code for the NJ OAG Law Enforcement Officer Diversity API deployed at
`api.tor-gu.com/nj/officer_diversity/`.

It serves [njoagleod](https://github.com/tor-gu/njoagleod), a cleaned-up copy of the NJ
Attorney General's [Law Enforcement Officer Diversity](https://www.njoag.gov/policerecruiting/)
data: officers for 2021 to 2025, and applicants and agency hiring and promotion practices
for 2022 to 2025. Field names and values are the same as in the R package; see it for more
details on the underlying dataset.

## Try it out

### OpenAPI/Swagger
There is an OpenAPI/swagger document deployed [here](https://tor-gu.com/apis/njoagleod.html)
that you can play with. The spec is `officer-diversity-openapi.yaml`.

### Endpoints
All under `/nj/officer_diversity`:

| Endpoint | R equivalent | Filters |
|---|---|---|
| `/officers` | the `officer` table | every column but `officer_count` |
| `/applicants` | the `applicant` table | every column but `applicant_count` |
| `/counts/officers?by=` | `count(officer, ..., wt = officer_count)` | as `/officers` |
| `/counts/applicants?by=` | `count(applicant, ..., wt = applicant_count)` | as `/applicants` |
| `/agency_practices` | the `agency_practice` table | every column |
| `/agency_practices/{year}/{agency_id}` | one row of `agency_practice` | |

`/officers` and `/applicants` are count tables: each row is a combination of year, agency
and characteristics, with the number of people who share it. **Counting rows counts
combinations, not people**, so use `/counts/*` or sum the count field. `by` takes 1 to 4
columns, comma-separated.

### Sample code
Each endpoint returns paginated results, with a `"next"` url in the `"links"` section
indicating that there are more results to be retrieved.

This is illustrated in the python code below, which loads the number of officers by year
and race into a
[pandas DataFrame](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.html).
```{python}
import json
import requests
import pandas as pd

API_ROOT = r.API_ROOT
DIVERSITY = f"{API_ROOT}/nj/officer_diversity"


def load_as_df(url):
    """Retrieve entire dataset at url and return as a dataframe"""
    # Get the first page
    resp = requests.get(url)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    resp_json = json.loads(resp.content.decode('utf-8'))
    df = pd.DataFrame(resp_json["data"])

    # Keep retrieving pages while there is a 'next' link
    while "next" in resp_json["links"]:
        resp = requests.get(resp_json["links"]["next"])
        resp.raise_for_status()
        resp_json = json.loads(resp.content.decode('utf-8'))
        df = pd.concat([df, pd.DataFrame(resp_json["data"])], ignore_index=True)
    return df


by_race = load_as_df(f"{DIVERSITY}/counts/officers?by=year,officer_race")
by_race_wide = (by_race.assign(officer_race=by_race["officer_race"].fillna("(not reported)"))
                .pivot(index="officer_race", columns="year", values="count")
                .rename(columns=str).reset_index())
```
```{r echo=FALSE}
library(reticulate)
knitr::kable(py$by_race_wide)
```

#### Agency names
Records carry `agency_id` only. Names, counties and the rest come from the
[njlea API](https://tor-gu.com/apis/njlea.html), joined on `agency_id`. Here are the ten
largest agencies of 2025, with their share of female officers:
```{python}
officers_2025 = load_as_df(f"{DIVERSITY}/counts/officers?by=agency_id,officer_gender&year=2025")
agencies_2025 = load_as_df(f"{API_ROOT}/nj/lea/agencies/2025")

totals = officers_2025.groupby("agency_id")["count"].sum().rename("officers")
female = (officers_2025[officers_2025["officer_gender"] == "Female"]
          .set_index("agency_id")["count"].rename("female"))
largest = (pd.concat([totals, female], axis=1).fillna({"female": 0}).reset_index()
           .assign(pct_female=lambda d: (100 * d["female"] / d["officers"]).round(1))
           .merge(agencies_2025[["agency_id", "agency_name", "county"]], on="agency_id")
           .nlargest(10, "officers")
           [["agency_name", "county", "officers", "pct_female"]])
```
```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(py$largest, row.names = FALSE)
```

#### Applicants
`/counts/applicants` works the same way. Here are the outcomes of applications by year:
```{python}
outcomes = load_as_df(f"{DIVERSITY}/counts/applicants?by=year,outcome")
outcomes_wide = (outcomes.assign(outcome=outcomes["outcome"].fillna("(not reported)"))
                 .pivot(index="outcome", columns="year", values="count")
                 .rename(columns=str).reset_index())
```
```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(py$outcomes_wide)
```

#### Agency practices
`/agency_practices` has each agency's answers about how it hires and promotes officers.
Every answer is also a filter, so `meta.record_count` says how many agencies gave it:
```{python}
url = f"{DIVERSITY}/agency_practices?year=2025&hiring_civil_service=true&page_size=1"
civil_service_agencies = requests.get(url).json()["meta"]["record_count"]
```
```{r echo=FALSE}
cat(py$civil_service_agencies, "agencies report that Civil Service governs their hiring in 2025.")
```

#### Use of force
The `agency_id` is the same one
[njoaguof-api](https://tor-gu.com/apis/njoaguof.html) uses, so use-of-force incidents can be
set against the size of each agency's force. Here are 2024 incidents per 100 officers, by
number of officers. Incidents of agencies with no officers in this data are left out.
```{python}
officers_2024 = load_as_df(f"{DIVERSITY}/counts/officers?by=agency_id&year=2024")
incidents_2024 = load_as_df(f"{API_ROOT}/nj/use_of_force/counts/incidents?by=agency_id&year=2024")

rates = (officers_2024.rename(columns={"count": "officers"})
         .merge(incidents_2024.rename(columns={"count": "incidents"}), on="agency_id", how="left")
         .fillna({"incidents": 0})
         .assign(size=lambda d: pd.cut(d["officers"], [0, 25, 100, 500, 100000],
                                       labels=["1-25", "26-100", "101-500", "over 500"])))
by_size = (rates.groupby("size", observed=True)
           .agg(agencies=("agency_id", "size"), officers=("officers", "sum"),
                incidents=("incidents", "sum"))
           .astype({"incidents": int})
           .assign(incidents_per_100=lambda d: (100 * d["incidents"] / d["officers"]).round(1))
           .reset_index())
by_size["size"] = by_size["size"].astype(str)
```
```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(py$by_size)
```

#### Caveats
The data is as reported by each agency, and some agency-years look incomplete. Nothing is
corrected. Lakewood PD, for example, reports far fewer officers in 2022 and 2025:
```{python}
lakewood = load_as_df(f"{DIVERSITY}/counts/officers?by=year&agency_id=NJLEA0401")
```
```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(py$lakewood)
```

The promotion columns are almost entirely `null` in 2021, so don't read `null` as "no":
```{python}
promoted = load_as_df(f"{DIVERSITY}/counts/officers?by=year,promoted")
promoted_wide = (promoted.assign(promoted=promoted["promoted"].map(
                     {True: "true", False: "false"}).fillna("null"))
                 .pivot(index="year", columns="promoted", values="count")
                 .reset_index())
```
```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(py$promoted_wide)
```

## Deploying
This API is implemented as an [AWS SAM](https://aws.amazon.com/serverless/sam/)
application: one Lambda function serves every route, with the data packaged in it. A
deployment has three parts:

1. The lambda layer [layer_torguapi](https://github.com/tor-gu/layer_torguapi) (version
   11 or later), which needs to be deployed separately.
2. The data: CSV exports of a tagged [njoagleod](https://github.com/tor-gu/njoagleod)
   release, committed in `data/`, and built into `diversity/data/` by `make data`.
3. The Lambda and API Gateway, defined in `template.yaml`.

### Data
`data/` holds the njoagleod tables and `SOURCE`, which records the release they were
exported from. The export also writes R's own `dplyr::count()` results to
`tests/parity/expected/`, which the parity test requires the API to reproduce, along with
the tables themselves. To export a release (this needs R and the `remotes` package; the
release is installed into a temporary library) and build the Lambda's data:
```
make export_data REF=v2.0.0
make data
```
`diversity/data/` holds one file of int32s per column and `labels.json`, so a request loads
only the columns it uses. It is not committed; CI builds it with `make data` before testing
and before `sam build`.

### Data update
1. `make export_data REF=<new release>`, and review the diff in `data/`.
2. `make data parity_test example_test`. The spec's examples, its enums and years, and
   this README (then `make knit`) may need updating; the example test shows the new values.
3. Push to `dev`, check the dev API, then merge to `main`.

### Development
```
make venv          # .venv with the test, style and spec tools
make style unit_test
make data example_test parity_test
make apigateway_spec   # the spec for API Gateway, without examples
```
The unit tests import the torguapi layer from `./torguapi`; `scripts/fetch_torguapi.sh`
downloads it.

### Direct deploy
The application can be deployed directly using the SAM CLI:
```
make data apigateway_spec
sam build
sam deploy --stack-name MyStackName                                                         \
           --capabilities CAPABILITY_IAM                                                    \
           --resolve-s3                                                                     \
           --parameter-overrides                                                            \
                TorguapiLayerArn=arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:layer:layer_torguapi \
                TorguapiLayerVersion=11                                                     \
                ApiRoot=https://api.example.com                                             \
                DataVersion=$(sed -n 's/^version=//p' data/SOURCE)
```
Replace the `TorguapiLayerXXX` params with the values derived from the `layer_torguapi`
deployment.

The `ApiRoot` value is used only for generating the values in `"links"` in the JSON reply.
On `api.tor-gu.com`, the relationship between the publicly facing API URL and the API
Gateway endpoints is configured in
[torgu-api-cloudfront](https://github.com/tor-gu/torgu-api-cloudfront).

To deploy a second environment alongside the first, give it a resource name prefix (I use
`dev-`) with the `EnvPrefix` template parameter.

### Using GitHub Actions
`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` deploys from GitHub: a push to `dev` deploys the dev
stack and runs the integration tests against it, and a merge to `main` deploys prod. It
assumes AWS roles through GitHub's OIDC provider; the roles are defined in
`infra/github/` (Terraform).
